title: US equity markets closed — Good Friday (falls BEFORE quarter-end in 2027)
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its holiday table by this session. Against the year headers, the 'Good Friday' row parses exactly as ['Friday, April 3', 'Friday, March 26', 'Friday, April 14'] for 2026 / 2027 / 2028 — i.e. the NYSE is closed Friday 2027-03-26. Independently reproduced by computing Easter with the anonymous Gregorian algorithm (Easter 2027 = 2027-03-28, so Good Friday = 2027-03-26; the same computation returns 2026-04-03 for 2026, matching the page). Filed estimate on two counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: DISCOVERED during the opex-2027-03-19 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and it is the first market-CLOSURE entry on this calendar. Why a day the market is shut earns a row: Easter 2027 is unusually early, so Good Friday lands in MARCH, between the 2027-03-19 quarterly triple witching and quarter-end — the configuration that changes the shape of both. The post-witching window normally runs 5 sessions to the following Friday; here it runs 4 (Mon 03-22 through Thu 03-25), and the quarter's final week is a 3-session stub (Mon 03-29, Tue 03-30, Wed 03-31). So the documented post-witching 'unpin' and the quarter-end rebalancing flows are compressed into fewer sessions than the same corridor carries in a normal quarter. In 2026 by contrast Good Friday was 04-03, safely inside Q2 and after quarter-end, which is the usual arrangement. Impact LOW and structural only: a closed session moves nothing by itself and no house playbook is calendar-keyed — it changes how many sessions the flows around it have to clear in, never direction. HONEST LIMIT ON THE KIND FIELD: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no slot for an exchange-schedule event, so this is filed 'sector' — the same kind the S&P rebalance market-structure entries use — which is the least-wrong option rather than a right one. Worth a follow-up on whether the union needs a 'market-structure' member; not this lane's call to make.
